intro.name: The patient
intro.text:
A villager, (patient), has been brought to the hospital in serious condition. The healers believe that (patient.he/she) is suffering from {A}, but they cannot agree on what to do next.
(Healer1) believes that the best course of action is {B}. (Healer2) disagrees, arguing that {C}.
To make matters worse, the village has a rule requiring {RULE}.
The rule was intended to protect the villagers. But in this case, following it might not be the same as doing what seems compassionate.

rule.text: The healers follow the village's procedure, even though it may take precious time. (Healer1) is {relieved|frustrated|anxious}. (Healer2) insists that rules exist for a reason.

r1.text: The approval arrives in time. The patient receives treatment.

r2.text: The rule prevents a dangerous and poorly understood treatment. The healers use a safer alternative.

r3.text: The delay causes a serious disagreement among the healers. By the time approval arrives, the patient's condition has changed.

r4.text: The healers discover that the rule was never intended for emergencies. {@Chief} clarifies it for future cases.

exception.text: The healers explain the situation to {@chief} and request permission to depart from the usual procedure. {@Chief} {listens carefully|looks deeply troubled|asks a great many questions}.

e1.text: {@Chief} grants an exception after hearing the medical evidence and the patient's wishes.

e2.text: {@Chief} refuses, fearing that an exception would be unfair to other villagers. The healers seek another acceptable treatment.

e3.text: {@Chief} admits that (leader.he/she) does not understand the medicine well enough to decide alone. The healers are asked to explain their reasoning before the council.

e4.text: {@Chief} authorizes emergency treatment, then orders a review of the village's laws so the same dilemma is less likely to recur.

voice.text: The healers explain the available treatments, their risks, and the uncertainties. They listen to what (patient) wants, or consult (patient.his/her) appropriate representative if (patient.he/she) cannot decide.

v1.text: (Patient) accepts the proposed treatment after asking several difficult questions.

v2.text: (Patient) refuses the risky treatment and chooses a less aggressive approach. The healers respect the informed decision.

v3.text: The patient cannot communicate, but a trusted representative describes (patient.his/her) previously expressed wishes.

v4.text: The patient asks for time to speak with loved ones. If medically possible, the healers give (patient.him/her) that time.

v5.text: The patient says, "I don't want everyone arguing about me as though I'm not here." The healers fall silent and listen.

council.text: The healers gather their colleagues to review the evidence, consider the patient's wishes, and decide what can be justified.

c1.text: The healers reach a consensus after reviewing the available evidence.

c2.text: The healers disagree, but identify a reasonable compromise that respects the patient's wishes.

c3.text: One healer admits that (healer3.he/she) was mistaken about an important detail. The others thank (healer3.him/her) for speaking up.

c4.text: The discussion reveals that two patients need the same scarce medicine. The healers use consistent clinical criteria rather than favoritism to decide how it should be allocated.

c5.text: The council remains divided. The healers document the uncertainty and choose a defensible course of action.

recovery.name: Full recovery
recovery.text:
After several difficult days, (patient)'s condition begins to improve. The fever subsides, (patient.his/her) strength returns, and the healers are finally able to breathe a sigh of relief.
(patient.He/She) eventually makes a full recovery. The village celebrates quietly, grateful that the treatment worked.

disability.name: Lasting effects
disability.text:
(Patient) survives, but the illness or injury has lasting effects. (patient.He/She) now has {reduced mobility in one limb|persistent weakness|difficulty with certain tasks|a lasting impairment that requires assistance}.
The healers explain what they know and what remains uncertain. The village helps (patient.him/her) adapt, making room for (patient.his/her) needs without treating (patient.him/her) as helpless.
(Patient) {returns to familiar work in a different way|learns a new skill|accepts help from friends|teaches others something about patience and perseverance}.

text_only.reason: rule 9: no game has a lasting disability; the source itself says to apply one only if the patcher supports it coherently (L1623-1624)
one of four story endings, not a skill reward

death.name: Death
death.text:
Despite the healers' efforts, (patient) grows weaker. One evening, (patient.he/she) dies.
The village is devastated. (Healer1) wonders whether another decision might have changed the outcome. (Healer2) reminds (healer1.him/her) that uncertainty cannot always be eliminated.
The villagers gather to remember (patient). Some are angry. Some are silent. Others simply sit together.
The healers review the case carefully - not to find someone to blame automatically, but to understand whether anything could have been done differently.
